name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3465
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.” Or watch this video.

clue.text: Provide food and support for insect

blocks.note: to cater is to supply food for an event
joins the two pieces
a pillar is a column that holds something up

explanation.surface: Someone is told to feed and prop up a bug, as if keeping a pet insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar is the larva of a butterfly or moth, an insect in its juvenile stage.

clue.text: Legal action in polite attire?

blocks.note: the setter's reading: a lawsuit between private parties, not a criminal case
the surface reading: courteous clothing, taking each word of the phrase literally

explanation.walkthrough: Read the two words of the answer literally: polite is the adjective and attire is a set of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A civil suit is a lawsuit brought by one private party against another, as opposed to a prosecution.

clue.text: Race winner's fast pace uphill, showing equilibrium after shedding outer garments

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means reading from the bottom up
shedding the outer layers strips off the first and last letters

blocks.note: a trot is a brisk running pace
something showing equilibrium is poised, held in balance

explanation.surface: A runner climbing a hill at speed stays balanced while stripping off layers.
explanation.walkthrough: The race is Aesop's fable of the tortoise and the hare, won by the slow tortoise; the pun is that the clue gives the winner a fast pace.
explanation.definitionFit: In Aesop's fable the tortoise beats the overconfident hare, so it is the famous race winner.

clue.text: Unrestrained anger, lacking the final bit of inhibition!

definitions.text: Unrestrained anger, lacking the final bit of inhibition!

indicators.text: lacking the final bit of inhibition
indicators.note: the final bit of inhibition is its last letter, which the word must go without
letters that are unrestrained run loose and can take any order

blocks.note: taken as written before losing a letter

explanation.surface: Fury running wild without the last trace of self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter of inhibition is N, so anger drops its N before the rearrangement. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage is violent, uncontrolled anger, exactly anger that has lost all inhibition.

clue.text: Booze in Spielberg movie about Eno

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the film's title wraps around the musician

blocks.note: taken as written
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film about an alien
Brian Eno, the musician and producer

explanation.surface: A drinks scene in a Spielberg film about the ambient musician Eno.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eno' gives his first name, not his surname. 'Booze' looks like a verb but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriant is anything that intoxicates, such as alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Advance by Confederate general sounds forlorn

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by how the words are spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: an advance of money is a loan
joins the two pieces
Robert E. Lee led the Confederate armies in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A Civil War general's advance has a sad, lonely sound to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' tempts as a military push, matching the general; it is a loan of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely and forlorn both describe someone sad because they are alone or abandoned.

clue.text: Where the Lyonnais get water to sharpen razor's edge, at first

indicators.note: an edge is the outermost bit of something, here the single leading letter of the word
at first says this piece comes at the start, before the verb it accompanies

blocks.note: the leading letter of razor
to hone a blade is to sharpen it

explanation.surface: People in Lyon fetch water to keep a razor sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: Lyon, France's third city, sits where the Rhône and Saône meet, so its people draw water from the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is the river that flows through Lyon, the city of the Lyonnais.

clue.text: Partner's half of counterrevolution

indicators.note: half of the long word means only part of its letters are used, a stretch lying within it
counter means running the opposite way, so the stretch is read back to front

blocks.note: the front half of the word revolution, which follows counter

explanation.surface: A spouse is said to own half of an uprising against a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counterrevolution' looks like one word, but it splits: 'counter' turns round half of 'revolution'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover is a romantic partner, someone in an intimate relationship with another person.

clue.text: Book caught fire and raised welt — a portent

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: something that caught fire was lit
taken as written before it is turned round
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A volume burst into flames and left a raised scar, an ominous sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised welt' reads as a swollen mark on the skin; here 'raised' turns the word upward. The novel is Louisa May Alcott's, about the four March sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's 1868 novel, a classic of American literature.

clue.text: Where celebrities are often found: an eco-chamber?

blocks.note: the surface reading: the backstage lounge where guests wait before a show
the setter's reading: a punning echo chamber, a room that is environmentally friendly in colour and spirit

explanation.surface: A quip about celebrities living inside an echo chamber, but spelt with eco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eco-chamber' is a pun on echo chamber; a room that is eco is a room that is environmentally virtuous, described by one colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A green room is the lounge in a theatre or TV studio where performers and guests wait before going on.

clue.text: Hit man's crumpled up cable for a hateful person

indicators.note: something crumpled up is crushed out of shape, so its letters lose their order

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged
a cable is a thick rope

explanation.surface: An assassin crumples a cable meant to finish off someone he hates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit man' suggests a killer, but its letters are what gets crumpled.
explanation.definitionFit: A misanthrope hates and distrusts humankind in general, so is a hateful person in the sense of full of hate.

clue.text: Fat cat's last permit

indicators.note: last asks for only the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the final letter of cat
to permit something is to allow it

explanation.surface: Something about a wealthy fat cat's final licence or permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat cat' reads as one phrase for a rich man, but 'Fat' is the definition and 'cat' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, used for candles and soap.

clue.text: People making a choice to eat right (doughnuts, more or less)

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: those who cull pick out and select from a group
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Choosy people tucking into doughnuts, or something close to them.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes in after the first letter of the selectors. 'More or less' is there because a cruller is a twisted pastry rather than a true ring doughnut.
explanation.definitionFit: Crullers are twisted fried pastries, close cousins of the doughnut in American bakeries.

clue.text: State "Costello is McKellen" to actor in the lead

indicators.note: whatever is in the lead is at the very front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: Lou Costello was the comic partner of Bud Abbott
taken as written
Sir Ian McKellen, the British actor
the opening letter of actor

explanation.surface: Someone declares to a lead actor that Costello is played by McKellen, a casting announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor in the lead' gives just the leading letter of actor. 'Costello' wants to be Elvis, but it is Lou of Abbott and Costello.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is one of the fifty US states, on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Amusement in the morning hours? That's a contradiction for a Belgian or Greek ruler

indicators.note: in places the amusement inside the time of day around it

blocks.note: a.m. marks the hours before noon
a game is a pastime or amusement

blocks.clueFragment: That's a contradiction for a Belgian
blocks.note: a French-speaking Belgian contradicts with the French word for no

explanation.surface: A puzzle about morning entertainment being a contradiction, for a king of Belgium or Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belgian or Greek ruler' looks like one definition; 'Belgian' belongs to the wordplay, since many Belgians speak French. The ruler is the king of Mycenae in Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greek armies at Troy.

clue.text: Small joke twisted…

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: A little joke given a twist, with the ellipsis promising the sentence goes on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay; 'twisted' is the definition, not a signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun is the past tense of spin, meaning turned or twisted, as yarn is spun.

clue.text: Heavily step up, clutching open fabric for tablecloth alternative

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom to the top
clutching means holding tight, so one piece is gripped inside the other

blocks.note: to stamp is to bring the foot down heavily
lace is a fine fabric full of holes

explanation.surface: Someone stomps upward, gripping an openwork cloth instead of covering the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Placemats sit under each diner's plate instead of one cloth covering the whole table.

clue.text: Productive territory on the upswing, getting one over terrible flu

indicators.note: something on the upswing is rising, which in a down clue reads from the bottom up
getting means taking in, so the reversed word receives a letter into it
something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: turf is a patch of territory, as in a gang's turf
the Roman numeral for one
the three letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fertile region is on the rise and has shaken off a bad bout of influenza.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the first part sits on top of the shuffled illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruitful land bears plenty of crops, so it is productive.

clue.text: …with phone-company unit

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
AT&T is the big American telephone company, ampersand dropped

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a small joke spun out together with a branch of the phone company.
explanation.walkthrough: AT&T, the American Telephone and Telegraph Company, loses its ampersand in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The watt is the SI unit of power, one joule per second.

clue.text: Frame that is ruined as a consequence

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A picture frame gets wrecked as a result of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath is the result or period following an event, especially a bad one.

clue.text: Foretells the end of summer in nearly a month

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter alone
nearly means not quite all, so the month loses its last letter
in puts the single letter inside the shortened month

blocks.note: August is the eighth month
the final letter of summer

explanation.surface: Summer's end is predicted for late August.
explanation.walkthrough: The month chosen is the one when summer ends, which makes the surface feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to predict or be a sign of the future, as ancient Roman augurs did.

clue.text: Jockey is a guy backing theatrical program of skits, songs, and dances

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the show's name is read from its end

blocks.note: a guy is a man

blocks.clueFragment: theatrical program of skits, songs, and dances
blocks.note: a revue is a stage show of sketches, songs and dance numbers

explanation.surface: A jockey is described as a man who funds a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' looks like a rider but is a verb, as in jockeying for position; 'backing' looks like financial support. The American spelling is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To jockey is to manoeuvre skilfully for advantage, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Rising, I see tin chip

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading the letters from the bottom up

blocks.note: oh is said when you understand, like I see
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone sees a piece of tin flying upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, usually served with melted cheese.

clue.text: Eatery with zero cash

blocks.note: a diner is a casual American restaurant
the figure zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A restaurant with no money in the till.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinero is the Spanish word for money, borrowed into American slang for cash.

clue.text: Swiss artist's modeling material discussed

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so the word is heard rather than seen

blocks.note: clay is what sculptors model with

explanation.surface: Talk about the sculpting medium a Swiss painter worked with.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter's name is pronounced like the material in German.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Klee was a Swiss-born painter of the early twentieth century, associated with the Bauhaus.

clue.text: In Northern California, crank is awake during the night

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the turning word sits within the region's name

blocks.note: NoCal is the informal short name for the northern part of the state
to crank a handle is to turn it

explanation.surface: A grouchy eccentric in northern California keeps late hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crank' tempts as a noun for an oddball; here it is the verb for turning a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal creature is active at night and sleeps by day.

clue.text: Ironclad escape for 7A

indicators.note: being clad means being covered, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: the first half of this word is iron, and Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
on the lam means on the run, so a lam is an escape

explanation.surface: An unbreakable getaway plan for a lover, as in a secret affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ironclad' splits into iron and clad. The definition sends you to 7-across, LOVER; LAM is American slang for flight from the law.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former sweetheart, so a flame is a lover.

clue.text: Filmmaker's building extension in roughly all four directions

indicators.note: in puts the extension within the run of letters that follows it

blocks.note: or so means approximately
the four compass points north, west, east, south
an ell is a wing built at right angles onto a house

explanation.surface: A director's house has an addition sprawling roughly in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass letters are taken in the order N, W, E, S, and the extension goes between W and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles directed and starred in Citizen Kane, one of cinema's most famous films.
